title: That was the once
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The tech, told the dimes are gone, runs the week free. Wood says he said once. The tech says that was the portfolio; this is the strip. Different once. Wood doesn't argue. He's learning which arguments the strip needs.

panels.composition: The print shop. WOOD with the strips and no money, saying so with his hands. The TECH. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a young man at a print shop counter showing empty hands to a technician while a small dog waits, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The tech, already loading the strips.

balloons.text: That was the portfolio. This is the strip.

image.prompt: a print technician loading comic strips onto a copier's glass without looking up, black and white, no words
a young man deciding not to argue, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The copies stacking. The tech not taking anything for them. Wood's hand on the stack like it's a dog. He's learning which arguments the strip needs. Not this one.

image.prompt: photocopies stacking in a tray as a young man rests his hand on them, a technician turning away, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Different once.' The argument the strip doesn't need.
